key_insight: A two-stage AI system can predict breast cancer response to neoadjuvant therapy by first inferring transcriptome activity from biopsy histology, then combining it with clinical features.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this approach could help identify patients most likely to achieve pathological complete response and support more tailored treatment planning.
method: Trained a first-stage model on histopathology to infer transcriptome signals using 8,742 patients across 32 cancer types.
Built a second-stage predictor for pCR from inferred expression plus clinical variables in 1,080 breast cancer patients from five cohorts.
Evaluated performance in 1,412 patients from nine cohorts and compared against histopathology-only and clinical-only baselines.
evidence_signal: The model achieved a pooled AUROC of 0.79 (95% CI, 0.73-0.85) in external evaluation and remained stable across molecular subtypes, intratumoral sampling, and limited biopsy tissue.
watch_item: Although promising, this is a retrospective multi-cohort study and prospective validation is still needed before routine clinical use.
paper_title: Transcriptome-informed multi-modal AI for predicting neoadjuvant therapy response from breast cancer biopsies
